page.layout: One printed page, right-hand side of the opening. Top: running head "VARIA POEMATA" with page number 168 at the head. Main text in one column: a verse block in italic, then a rule, a centred title "AD D. BEZAM, V. CL.", then a verse poem. Catchword "Et" at lower right. No margin notes.

l.i: Nec gerit ille hominis pectus, qui vincula verae
Credit amicitiae, nedum quae Numinis ipsa
Legitimi conftructa manu sunt foedera lecti,
Et certe quanto est multis pretiosius istud
Certius est tanto divini pignus amoris,
Dissolui quod vix sine vulnere possit acerbo,
Sive suos Deus exploret, seu vindice dextra
His doctus monitis, sic attamen ipse dolebis
Beza quidem, at certa ratione modoque dolebis,
Et tua deficies deinceps quid postulet aetas.
Haec ille, admonitu cuius meliora secutus,
Feci, quod te etiam forsan fecisse juvabit.

main_text.l: ERGO mihi nunquam rumpenda silentia? nunquam
Siccine nos sacri cessare ad carmina vatis?
Beza fave, longoque volens ignosce dolori:
Mœrorisque tegi specie ne rere veternum.
Ah quoties tentata suo mihi tibia plectro
Triste melos potuit tantum, & lachrymabile carmẽ!
Ah quoties paucos meditor dum scribere versus.
Obstupui, atque imo suspiria pectore duxi!

page.notes: The swash letter in "Beza" (lines 9 and 3 of the second part) is a decorative form; read as Beza. The "carmẽ" line-end has a tilde over the e, read as printed. Long s is normalised to s throughout. The first letter of the poem is a large initial E, joined as ERGO. No marginal notes or stains affecting the text.
